newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias creditors yet to recieve interest.
newsitem.headline: Victorias creditors yet to recieve interest.

text.p: A sum of 110 million pesos paid by Victorias Milling Co as interest payment towards debts was not distributed as the money received was retained by one bank, one of the creditors said on Monday.
The official, who did not want to be named, said the bank nominated to receive the interest payments on behalf of the 32 creditors had not transferred it to the other banks.
"Victorias kept their part of the bargain. They put the money in ... that bank turns around and sets off the funds against some of its loans of 120 or 130 million pesos," the official said.
Another bank confirmed a problem with the disbursement of interest payments but said it was caused by operational problems.
"There is problem with respect to the funds transfer," Honorio Reyes-Lao, senior vice president of China Bank, another of the creditor banks said.

He said more than one bank was nominated to receive the interest payments last Friday but the transfer had not taken place as the receving banks were still seeking the approval from their managements to disburse the money to the other banks.
Lao said the creditors committee was in a meeting on Monday afternoon to discuss the issue and prevent a similar hitch from occuring again.
On Friday, an official of cash-strapped Victorias said the company has enough funds to make interest payments on its 4.423 billion pesos debts due that day.
"The check is ready for deposit. We have enough funds to update payments on all our 32 creditors," the Victorias official who requested not to be named told Reuters on Friday.
Victorias, the country's largest sugar miller, has obtained a 90-day reprieve on principal payments on its debt.
